exercises.heading: Section 5.5 Exercises
exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, evaluate the triple integrals $$\iiint\limits_{B}{f(x,y,z)dV}$$ over the solid $$B.$$

problem.paragraph: $$f(x,y,z) = z,$$ $$B = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| x^{2} + y^{2} \leq 9,x \geq 0,y \geq 0,0 \leq z \leq 1 \right\}$$
$$f(x,y,z) = xz^{2},$$ $$B = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| x^{2} + y^{2} \leq 16,x \geq 0,y \leq 0,-1 \leq z \leq 1 \right\}$$
$$f(x,y,z) = xy,$$ $$B = \left\{ (x,y,z) \middle| x^{2} + y^{2} \leq 1,x \geq 0,y \geq 0,x \leq y,-1 \leq z \leq 1 \right\}$$
$$f(x,y,z) = x^{2} + y^{2},$$ $$B = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| x^{2} + y^{2} \leq 4,x \geq 0,x \leq y,0 \leq z \leq 3 \right\}$$
$$f(x,y,z) = e^{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}},$$ $$B = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| 1 \leq x^{2} + y^{2} \leq 4,y \leq 0,x \leq y\sqrt{3},2 \leq z \leq 3 \right\}$$
$$f(x,y,z) = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}},$$ $$B = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| 1 \leq x^{2} + y^{2} \leq 9,y \leq 0,0 \leq z \leq 1 \right\}$$

list.item: Let $$B$$ be a cylindrical shell with inner radius $$a,$$ outer radius $$b,$$ and height $$c,$$ where $$0 < a < b$$ and $$c > 0.$$ Assume that a function $$F$$ defined on $$B$$ can be expressed in cylindrical coordinates as $$F(x,y,z) = f(r) + h(z),$$ where $$f$$ and $$h$$ are differentiable functions. If $$\int\limits_{a}^{b}{\widetilde{f}(r)dr = 0}$$ and $$\widetilde{h}(0) = 0,$$ where $$\widetilde{f}$$ and $$\widetilde{h}$$ are antiderivatives of $$f$$ and $$h,$$ respectively, show that $${\iiint\limits_{B}{F\left( {x,y,z} \right)dV}} = 2\pi c\left( {b\widetilde{f}(b) - a\widetilde{f}(a)} \right) + \pi\left( {b^{2} - a^{2}} \right)\widetilde{h}(c).$$

Use the previous result to show that $${\iiint\limits_{B}\left( {z + \sin \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}} \right)}dx dy dz = 6\pi^{2}\left( {\pi - 2} \right),$$ where $$B$$ is a cylindrical shell with inner radius $$\pi,$$ outer radius $$2\pi,$$ and height $$2.$$

Let $$B$$ be a cylindrical shell with inner radius $$a,$$ outer radius $$b,$$ and height $$c,$$ where $$0 < a < b$$ and $$c > 0.$$ Assume that a function $$F$$ defined on $$B$$ can be expressed in cylindrical coordinates as $$F(x,y,z) = f(r)g(\theta)h(z),$$ where $$f,g, \text{and} h$$ are differentiable functions. If $${\int\limits_{a}^{b}{\widetilde{f}(r)dr = 0}},$$ where $$\widetilde{f}$$ is an antiderivative of $$f,$$ show that $${\iiint\limits_{B}{F\left( {x,y,z} \right)dV}} = \left\lbrack {b\widetilde{f}(b) - a\widetilde{f}(a)} \right\rbrack \left\lbrack {\widetilde{g}(2\pi) - \widetilde{g}(0)} \right\rbrack \left\lbrack {\widetilde{h}(c) - \widetilde{h}(0)} \right\rbrack,$$ where $$\widetilde{g}$$ and $$\widetilde{h}$$ are antiderivatives of $$g$$ and $$h,$$ respectively.

Use the previous result to show that $${\iiint\limits_{B}{z \sin \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}}}dx dy dz = -12\pi^{2},$$ where $$B$$ is a cylindrical shell with inner radius $$\pi,$$ outer radius $$2\pi,$$ and height $$2.$$

exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, the boundaries of the solid $$E$$ are given in cylindrical coordinates. Let $$f (r,\theta,z)$$ be the corresponding function in cylindrical coordinates.

list.item: Define the region in cylindrical coordinates.
Convert the integral $$\iiint\limits_{Ε}g(x,y,z)dV$$ to cylindrical coordinates.

problem.paragraph: $$E$$ is inside the right circular cylinder $$r = 4 \sin \theta,$$ above the $$r\theta$$ -plane, and inside the sphere $$r^{2} + z^{2} = 16.$$

solution.paragraph: a. $$E={(r,\theta ,z)|0\le \theta \le \pi ,0\le r\le 4sin\theta ,0\le z\le 16-r2};E={(r,\theta ,z)|0\le \theta \le \pi ,0\le r\le 4sin\theta ,0\le z\le 16-r2};$$ b. $$\int 0\pi \int 04sin\theta \int 016-r2f(r,\theta ,z)rdzdrd\theta \int 0\pi \int 04sin\theta \int 016-r2f(r,\theta ,z)rdzdrd\theta$$

problem.paragraph: $$E$$ is inside the right circular cylinder $$r = \cos \theta,$$ above the $$r\theta$$ -plane, and inside the sphere $$r^{2} + z^{2} = 9.$$

$$E$$ is located in the first octant and is bounded by the circular paraboloid $$z = 9 - 3r^{2},$$ the cylinder $$r = \sqrt{3},$$ and the plane $$r\left( {\cos \theta + \sin \theta} \right) = 20 - z.$$

solution.paragraph: a. $$E={(r,\theta ,z)|0\le \theta \le \pi 2,0\le r\le 3,9-3r2\le z\le 20-r(cos\theta +sin\theta )};E={(r,\theta ,z)|0\le \theta \le \pi 2,0\le r\le 3,9-3r2\le z\le 20-r(cos\theta +sin\theta )};$$ b. $$\int 0\pi /2\int 03\int 9-3r220-r(cos\theta +sin\theta )f(r,\theta ,z)rdzdrd\theta \int 0\pi /2\int 03\int 9-3r220-r(cos\theta +sin\theta )f(r,\theta ,z)rdzdrd\theta$$

problem.paragraph: $$E$$ is located in the first octant outside the circular paraboloid $$z = 10 - 2r^{2}$$ and inside the cylinder $$r = \sqrt{5}$$ and is bounded also by the planes $$z = 20$$ and $$\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}.$$

exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, the function $$g$$ and region $$E$$ are given in rectangular coordinates.

list.item: Express the region $$Ε$$ and the function $$g$$ in cylindrical coordinates. Let $$f(r,\theta,z)$$ be the corresponding function in cylindrical coordinates.
Convert the integral $${\iiint\limits_{E}{g\left( {x,y,z} \right)}}dV$$ to cylindrical coordinates and evaluate it.

problem.paragraph: $$g\left( {x,y,z} \right) = \frac{1}{x + 3},$$ $$E = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| 0 \leq x^{2} + y^{2} \leq 9,x \geq 0,y \geq 0,0 \leq z \leq x + 3 \right\}$$

solution.paragraph: a. $$E={(r,\theta ,z)|0\le r\le 3,0\le \theta \le \pi 2,0\le z\le rcos\theta +3},E={(r,\theta ,z)|0\le r\le 3,0\le \theta \le \pi 2,0\le z\le rcos\theta +3},$$ $$f(r,\theta ,z)=1rcos\theta +3;f(r,\theta ,z)=1rcos\theta +3;$$ b. $$\int 03\int 0\pi /2\int 0rcos\theta +3rrcos\theta +3dzd\theta dr=9\pi 4\int 03\int 0\pi /2\int 0rcos\theta +3rrcos\theta +3dzd\theta dr=9\pi 4$$

problem.paragraph: $$g\left( {x,y,z} \right) = x^{2} + y^{2},$$ $$E = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| 0 \leq x^{2} + y^{2} \leq 4,y \geq 0,0 \leq z \leq 3 - x \right\}$$
$$g\left( {x,y,z} \right) = x,$$ $$E = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| 1 \leq y^{2} + z^{2} \leq 9,0 \leq x \leq 9 - y^{2} - z^{2} \right\}$$

solution.paragraph: a. $$y=rcos\theta ,z=rsin\theta ,x=z,y=rcos\theta ,z=rsin\theta ,x=z,$$ $$E={(r,\theta ,z)|1\le r\le 3,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,0\le z\le 9-r2},f(r,\theta ,z)=z;E={(r,\theta ,z)|1\le r\le 3,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,0\le z\le 9-r2},f(r,\theta ,z)=z;$$ b. $$\int 13\int 02\pi \int 09-r2zrdzd\theta dr=256\pi 3\int 13\int 02\pi \int 09-r2zrdzd\theta dr=256\pi 3$$

problem.paragraph: $$g\left( {x,y,z} \right) = y,$$ $$E = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| 1 \leq x^{2} + z^{2} \leq 9,0 \leq y \leq 9 - x^{2} - z^{2} \right\}$$

exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, find the volume of the solid $$E$$ whose boundaries are given in rectangular coordinates.

problem.paragraph: $$E$$ is above the $$xy$$ -plane, inside the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 1,$$ and below the plane $$z = 1.$$
$$E$$ is below the plane $$z = 1$$ and inside the paraboloid $$z = x^{2} + y^{2}.$$
$$E$$ is bounded by the circular cone $$z = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}$$ and $$z = 1.$$
$$E$$ is located above the $$xy$$ -plane, below $$z = 1,$$ outside the one-sheeted hyperboloid $$x^{2} + y^{2} - z^{2} = 1,$$ and inside the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 2.$$
$$E$$ is located inside the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$$ and between the circular paraboloids $$z = 1 - x^{2} - y^{2}$$ and $$z = x^{2} + y^{2}.$$
$$E$$ is located inside the sphere $$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 1,$$ above the $$xy$$ -plane, and inside the circular cone $$z = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}.$$
$$E$$ is located inside the circular cone $$x^{2} + y^{2} = \left( {z - 1} \right)^{2}$$ and between the planes $$z = 0$$ and $$z = 2.$$

$$E$$ is located inside the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$$ , above the circular cone $$z = 1 - \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}$$ , and below the circular paraboloid $$z = 1 + x^{2} + y^{2}$$ , and between the planes $$z = 0$$ and $$z = 2$$ .

[T] Use a computer algebra system (CAS) to graph the solid whose volume is given by the iterated integral in cylindrical coordinates $${\int\limits_{-{\pi/2}}^{\pi/2} {\int\limits_{0}^{1} {\int\limits_{r^{2}}^{r}{r dz dr d\theta}}}}.$$ Find the volume $$V$$ of the solid. Round your answer to four decimal places.

[T] Use a CAS to graph the solid whose volume is given by the iterated integral in cylindrical coordinates $${\int\limits_{0}^{\pi/2} {\int\limits_{0}^{1} {\int\limits_{r^{4}}^{r}{r dz dr d\theta}}}}.$$ Find the volume $$V$$ of the solid Round your answer to four decimal places.

Convert the integral $$\int\limits_{0}^{1} {\int\limits_{-\sqrt{1 - y^{2}}}^{\sqrt{1 - y^{2}}} {\int\limits_{x^{2} + y^{2}}^{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}}{xz dz dx dy}}}$$ into an integral in cylindrical coordinates.

solution.paragraph: $$\int 0 1 \int 0 \pi \int r 2 r z r 2 cos \theta d z d \theta d r \int 0 1 \int 0 \pi \int r 2 r z r 2 cos \theta d z d \theta d r$$

problem.paragraph: Convert the integral $${\int\limits_{0}^{2} {\int\limits_{0}^{y} {\int\limits_{0}^{1}\left( {xy + z} \right)}}}dz dx dy$$ into an integral in cylindrical coordinates.

exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, evaluate the triple integral $$\iiint\limits_{B}{f(x,y,z)dV}$$ over the solid $$B.$$

problem.paragraph: $$f(x,y,z) = 1,$$ $$B = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} \leq 90,z \geq 0 \right\}$$
$$f(x,y,z) = 1 - \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}},$$ $$B = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} \leq 9,y \geq 0,z \geq 0 \right\}$$
$$f(x,y,z) = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}},$$ $$B$$ is bounded above by the half-sphere $$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 9$$ with $$z \geq 0$$ and below by the cone $$z^{2} = x^{2} + y^{2}.$$
$$f(x,y,z) = z,$$ $$B$$ is bounded above by the half-sphere $$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 16$$ with $$z \geq 0$$ and below by the cone $$z^{2} = x^{2} + y^{2}.$$

Show that if $$F\left( {\rho,\theta,\varphi} \right) = f(\rho)g(\theta)h(\varphi)$$ is a continuous function on the spherical box $$B = \left\{ {\left. \left( {\rho,\theta,\varphi} \right) \right|a \leq \rho \leq b,\alpha \leq \theta \leq \beta,\gamma \leq \varphi \leq \psi} \right\},$$ then

$${\iiint\limits_{B}{F dV}} = \left( {\int\limits_{a}^{b}{\rho^{2}f(\rho)dr}} \right)\left( {\int\limits_{\alpha}^{\beta}{g(\theta)d\theta}} \right)\left( {\int\limits_{\gamma}^{\psi}{h(\varphi)\sin \varphi d\varphi}} \right).$$

list.item: A function $$F$$ is said to have spherical symmetry if it depends on the distance to the origin only, that is, it can be expressed in spherical coordinates as $$F\left( {x,y,z} \right) = f(\rho),$$ where $$\rho = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}.$$ Show that $${\iiint\limits_{B}{F(x,y,z)dV}} = 2\pi{\int\limits_{a}^{b}{\rho^{2}f(\rho)d\rho}},$$ where $$B$$ is the region between the upper concentric hemispheres of radii $$a$$ and $$b$$ centered at the origin, with $$0 < a < b$$ and $$F$$ a spherical function defined on $$B.$$

Use the previous result to show that $${\iiint\limits_{B}{\left( {x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}} \right)\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}} dV}} = 21\pi,$$ where $$B = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| 1 \leq x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} \leq 2,z \geq 0 \right\}.$$

Let $$B$$ be the region between the upper concentric hemispheres of radii a and b centered at the origin and situated in the first octant, where $$0 < a < b.$$ Consider F a function defined on B whose form in spherical coordinates $$\left( {\rho,\theta,\varphi} \right)$$ is $$F\left( {x,y,z} \right) = f(\rho)\cos \varphi.$$ Show that if $$g(a) = g(b) = 0$$ and $${\int\limits_{a}^{b}{h(\rho)d\rho = 0}},$$ then $${\iiint\limits_{B}{F(x,y,z)dV}} = \frac{\pi^{2}}{4}\left\lbrack {ah(a) - bh(b)} \right\rbrack,$$ where $$g$$ is an antiderivative of $$f$$ and $$h$$ is an antiderivative of $$g.$$

Use the previous result to show that $${\iiint\limits_{B}{\frac{z \cos \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}}{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}}dV}} = \frac{3\pi^{2}}{2},$$ where $$B$$ is the region between the upper concentric hemispheres of radii $$\pi$$ and $$2\pi$$ centered at the origin and situated in the first octant.

exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, the function $$g$$ and region $$E$$ are given in rectangular coordinates.

list.item: Express the region $$E$$ and the function $$g$$ in spherical coordinates. Let $$f(\rho, \theta, \varphi)$$ be the corresponding function in spherical coordinates
Convert the integral $${\iiint\limits_{E}{g\left( {x,y,z} \right)}}dV$$ to spherical coordinates and evaluate it.

problem.paragraph: $$g\left( {x,y,z} \right) = z;$$ $$E = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| 0 \leq x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} \leq 1,z \geq 0 \right\}$$
$$g\left( {x,y,z} \right) = x + y;$$ $$E = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| 1 \leq x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} \leq 4,z \geq 0,y \geq 0 \right\}$$

solution.paragraph: a. $$f(ρ,\theta ,\phi )=ρsin\phi (cos\theta +sin\theta ),f(ρ,\theta ,\phi )=ρsin\phi (cos\theta +sin\theta ),$$ $$E={(ρ,\theta ,\phi )|1\le ρ\le 2,0\le \theta \le \pi ,0\le \phi \le \pi 2};E={(ρ,\theta ,\phi )|1\le ρ\le 2,0\le \theta \le \pi ,0\le \phi \le \pi 2};$$ b. $$\int 0\pi \int 0\pi /2\int 12ρ3sin2\phi cos\theta +sin\theta =15\pi 8\int 0\pi \int 0\pi /2\int 12ρ3sin2\phi cos\theta +sin\theta =15\pi 8$$

problem.paragraph: $$g\left( {x,y,z} \right) = 2xy;$$ $$E = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}} \leq z \leq \sqrt{1 - x^{2} - y^{2}},x \geq 0,y \geq 0 \right\}$$
$$g\left( {x,y,z} \right) = z;$$ $$E = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} - 2z \leq 0,\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}} \leq z \right\}$$

solution.paragraph: a. $$f(ρ,\theta ,\phi )=ρcos\phi ;f(ρ,\theta ,\phi )=ρcos\phi ;$$ $$E={(ρ,\theta ,\phi )|0\le ρ\le 2cos\phi ,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,0\le \phi \le \pi 4};E={(ρ,\theta ,\phi )|0\le ρ\le 2cos\phi ,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,0\le \phi \le \pi 4};$$ b. $$\int 02\pi \int 0\pi /4\int 02cos\phi ρ3sin\phi cos\phi dρd\phi d\theta =7\pi 6\int 02\pi \int 0\pi /4\int 02cos\phi ρ3sin\phi cos\phi dρd\phi d\theta =7\pi 6$$

exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, find the volume of the solid $$E$$ whose boundaries are given in rectangular coordinates.

problem.paragraph: $$E = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}} \leq z \leq \sqrt{16 - x^{2} - y^{2}},x \geq 0,y \geq 0 \right\}$$
$$E = \left\{ \left( {x,y,z} \right) \middle| x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} - 2z \leq 0,\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}} \leq z \right\}$$

Use spherical coordinates to find the volume of the solid situated inside the sphere $$\rho = 1$$ and outside the sphere $$\rho = \cos \varphi,$$ with $$\varphi \in \left\lbrack {0,\frac{\pi}{2}} \right\rbrack.$$
Use spherical coordinates to find the volume of the ball $$\rho \leq 3$$ that is situated between the cones $$\varphi = \frac{\pi}{4} \text{and} \varphi = \frac{\pi}{3}.$$

Convert the integral $${\int\limits_{-4}^{4} {\int\limits_{-\sqrt{16 - y^{2}}}^{\sqrt{16 - y^{2}}} {\int\limits_{-\sqrt{16 - x^{2} - y^{2}}}^{\sqrt{16 - x^{2} - y^{2}}}\left( {x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}} \right)}}}dz dx dy$$ into an integral in spherical coordinates.

Convert the integral $${\int\limits_{0}^{4} {\int\limits_{0}^{\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}} {\int\limits_{-\sqrt{16 - x^{2} - y^{2}}}^{\sqrt{16 - x^{2} - y^{2}}}\left( {x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}} \right)^{2}}}}dz dy dx$$ into an integral in spherical coordinates.

solution.paragraph: $$\int 0 \pi / 2 \int 0 \pi \int 0 4 ρ 6 sin \phi d ρ d \phi d \theta \int 0 \pi / 2 \int 0 \pi \int 0 4 ρ 6 sin \phi d ρ d \phi d \theta$$

problem.paragraph: Convert the integral $$\int\limits_{-2\sqrt{2}}^{2\sqrt{2}} \int\limits_{- \sqrt{8 - x^{2}}}^{\sqrt{8 - x^{2}}} \int\limits_{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}}^{\sqrt{16 - x^{2} - y^{2}}}dz dy dx$$ into an integral in spherical coordinates and evaluate it.

[T] Use a CAS to graph the solid whose volume is given by the iterated integral in spherical coordinates $${\int\limits_{\pi/2}^{\pi} {\int\limits_{{5\pi}/6}^{\pi/6} {\int\limits_{0}^{2}{\rho^{2}\sin \varphi}}}} d\rho d\varphi d\theta.$$ Find the volume $$V$$ of the solid. Round your answer to three decimal places.

[T] Use a CAS to graph the solid whose volume is given by the iterated integral in spherical coordinates as $${\int\limits_{0}^{2\pi} {\int\limits_{\pi/4}^{3\pi/4} {\int\limits_{0}^{1}{\rho^{2}\sin \varphi}}}} d\rho d\varphi d\theta.$$ Find the volume $$V$$ of the solid. Round your answer to three decimal places.
[T] Use a CAS to evaluate the integral $${\iiint\limits_{E}\left( {x^{2} + y^{2}} \right)}dV$$ where $$E$$ lies above the paraboloid $$z = x^{2} + y^{2}$$ and below the plane $$z = 3y.$$

list.item: Evaluate the integral $${\iiint\limits_{E}{e^{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}}dV}},$$ where $$E$$ is bounded by the spheres $$4x^{2} + 4y^{2} + 4z^{2} = 1$$ and $$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 1.$$
Use a CAS to find an approximation of the previous integral. Round your answer to two decimal places.

problem.paragraph: Express the volume of the solid inside the sphere $$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 16$$ and outside the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 4$$ as triple integrals in cylindrical coordinates and spherical coordinates.

Express the volume of the solid inside the sphere $$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 16$$ and outside the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 4$$ that is located in the first octant as triple integrals in cylindrical coordinates and spherical coordinates.
The power emitted by an antenna has a power density per unit volume given in spherical coordinates by

$$p\left( {\rho,\theta,\varphi} \right) = \frac{P_{0}}{\rho^{2}}\cos^{2}\theta \sin^{4}\varphi,$$ where $$P_{0}$$ is a constant with units in watts. The total power within a sphere $$B$$ of radius $$r$$ meters is defined as $$P = {\iiint\limits_{B}{p\left( {\rho,\theta,\varphi} \right)}}dV.$$ Find the total power $$P$$ within a sphere of radius 20 meters.

Use the preceding exercise to find the total power within a sphere $$B$$ of radius 5 meters when the power density per unit volume is given by $$p\left( {\rho,\theta,\varphi} \right) = \frac{30}{\rho^{2}}\cos^{2}\theta \sin^{4}\varphi.$$

A charge cloud contained in a sphere $$B$$ of radius r centimeters centered at the origin has its charge density given by $$q\left( {x,y,z} \right) = k\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}\frac{\mu \text{C} }{ \text{cm} ^{3}},$$ where $$k > 0.$$ The total charge contained in $$B$$ is given by $$Q = {\iiint\limits_{B}{q\left( {x,y,z} \right)}}dV.$$ Find the total charge $$Q.$$

solution.paragraph: $$Q = k r 4 \pi \mu C Q = k r 4 \pi \mu C$$

problem.paragraph: Use the preceding exercise to find the total charge cloud contained in the unit sphere if the charge density is $$q\left( {x,y,z} \right) = 20\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}\frac{\mu \text{C} }{ \text{cm} ^{3}}.$$
